subject: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access & break-glass
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access & break-glass

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps on the access controls items you asked about:

- RBAC: Redwood supports role-based access with custom roles; default roles include Admin, Engineer, ReadOnly, Support. Fine-grained resource scoping by org/project/model is available.
- Least privilege: You can scope API tokens to specific routes (generate, embeddings) and set TTLs. We also have service accounts with limited permissions and session-scoped tokens.
- Support access / break-glass: Support access is off by default; customers can enable time-limited break-glass sessions with multi-approver workflows (SSO + manager approval). Break-glass sessions are logged and produce a tamper-evident audit trail.
- Audit & logging: All admin actions and model inference logs include actor, timestamp, request id, and affected resource. Retention is configurable at org level; default 90 days but we can support longer retention on Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency: Hosted regions in us/eu; Dedicated and Private deployments allow on-prem or VPC-only residency.

Attachments: I've attached a one-page summary and our RBAC design doc for your security team to review.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which roles you'd like to map to FinTrust groups (e.g., "ML Engineers", "SRE", "Support") — reply by EOD next Tue (9/15).
2) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Dev (cc'd) next week to walk through the console and the break-glass workflow.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our security team after I shared the summary:

1) For break-glass, can you confirm whether access requires an explicit approval from a second admin (we'd prefer multi-approver for elevated sessions)?
2) For audit logs, can we export logs to our SIEM (Splunk) in near real-time? Is there a webhook or syslog integration?
3) Regarding least privilege, does Redwood support attribute-based access (ABAC) or only RBAC? We have some resources that would benefit from attribute tagging.

Also want to include our InfoSec reviewer Anna on the thread — she'll take a look at the RBAC doc.

Can we do the technical deep-dive on Tue 9/15 at 10am PT? If Dev can make that time, we'll send a calendar invite.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up — RBAC, support access & break-glass

Hi Sarah — quick answers to your questions below, and I've attached a short tech note with screenshots: rbac_design_overview.pdf.

1) Break-glass multi-approver: yes — for Dedicated/Private we support configurable approval policies. You can require N-of-M approvers (SSO enforced). For Hosted we offer a two-step approval flow (primary admin + emergency approver) or integration with your approval workflow (OKTA/Workday/ServiceNow).

2) Log export / SIEM: we have a near real-time events API and can forward to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector (HEC) or to a syslog endpoint for Private deployments. We also support pushing logs to an S3 bucket which you can ingest. Latency is typically <30s for HEC in most regions.

3) ABAC support: Redwood's current model is RBAC-first with tag-based scoping on resources (resource tags can be used to approximate ABAC). Full ABAC policies are on our roadmap and we can share a timeline in the technical deep-dive.

Follow-ups included in the attached doc: implementation options for break-glass, sample SIEM integration snippet, and role mapping template.

Thanks — I can lead the deep-dive on Tue 9/15 10:00am PT. Please send the invite.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
